proof_checks: For a=b>=3 and primitive D=0, both indices vanish and the rank is a^2.
For D=1, the two indices sum to a and each is at most a, giving rank a^2+a.
For D=2, mu1<=a. Rank-one minimum vectors have degree(a+1)h, so h=0; the rank-two lower bound is a-1. Thus mu1 belongs to{0,a-1,a}.
For D>=3, mu1=0 gives rank a^2+a. Positive rank-one mu1 is at least a+1; rank-two mu1 is at least ceil(3(a-1)/2)>=a. Both positive indices therefore give full retained row rank a^2+2a.
Consequently a^2+2a-1 requires exactly D=2 and indices(a-1,a+1). Common-factor normalization remains essential.
Containment is restricted to quadratic-or-lower z-degree for a>3. Universal attainment is asserted only for a=b=3, with its existing proof.
code_checks: Exact sparse echelon elimination preserves the previous rank API. Descending pivot substitution constructs one coefficient-kernel vector.
Inspection verifies the full recurrence residual and exact minimum degree before computing Hankel rank from polynomial two-by-two minors.
The verified nonzero coefficient triple supplies a right kernel, so the Hankel rank is at most two; nonzero recurrence vectors make it at least one.
Polynomial coefficient maps retain all output coefficients. Degree D-1 and D nullity tests check the asserted left/right minimal-index totals.
New structural controls cover a=2 with no left indices, odd-valuation irreducibility including characteristic two, and a nonconstant height-one root below the rank-two threshold.
Universal a=3 controls use literal full source ranks plus exact off-block checks and Bareiss determinants; they do not assert larger-size attainment.
2050 source comparisons equals prior2010 plus24 structural source maps and16 spectrum source maps.
